title: Add Python "All"  and "Curated-All" repo's
description:
With some of the limitations around being able to specify install order when using pip, the current best practice recommendation is to use one combined python repository (that includes internal packages + PyPi) for mitigating security concerns around dependency confusion attacks. With the next package manager release including curated python repositories it would be great to have this as well! 

Best practices from Joe: 

 - https://positpbc.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PPM/pages/253296656/Package+Security+in+R+and+Python 

Posit products documentation: 

 - https://docs.posit.co/connect/admin/python/package-management/#specifying-a-package-repository
 - https://docs.posit.co/rsc/integration/rspm/#overriding-cran-with-package-manager

Stackoverflow discussing the install priority challenge with pip: 

 - https://stackoverflow.com/questions/67253141/python-pip-priority-order-with-index-url-and-extra-index-url

Python pip git issues and pep proposing a long term solution: 

 - https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8606
 - https://github.com/python/peps/blob/main/pep-0708.rst
 - https://discuss.python.org/t/pep-708-extending-the-repository-api-to-mitigate-dependency-confusion-attacks/24179

title: Upgrade session and colorado to Jammy
adjust additional packages to be installed in a separate library from base library
description:
the risk of adding to the base library install is that even when setting to explicit other library paths, this base setup will always persist, thus those packages will continue to pollute the namespace.

For example, after initializing a new project with renv it still shows 974:

```
> length(installed.packages()[,1])
[1] 974
```


```
# Bootstrapping renv 0.15.5 --------------------------------------------------
* Downloading renv 0.15.5 ... OK (downloaded source)
* Installing renv 0.15.5 ... Done!
* Successfully installed and loaded renv 0.15.5.
* Project '~/scratch' loaded. [renv 0.15.5]
> length(installed.packages()[,1])
[1] 974
> 
> .libPaths()
[1] "/usr/home/devin.pastoor/scratch/renv/library/R-4.2/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"
[2] "/opt/R/4.2.0/lib/R/library"                                            
> dir(.libPaths()[1])
[1] "renv"
> dir(.libPaths()[2])
  [1] "A3"                   "abc"                  "abc.data"             "ABC.RAP"              "ABCanalysis"         
  [6] "ABCoptim"             "ABCp2"                "ABHgenotypeR"         "abind"                "ABPS"                
 [11] "ACA"                  "ACDm"                 "acepack"              "ACEt"                 "acs"                 
 [16] "ACSWR"                "actuar"               "ada"                  "addinslist"           "additivityTests"     
 [21] "ade4"                 "AER"                  "akima"                "alabama"              "AlgDesign"           
 [26] "alphavantager"        "Amelia"               "AmesHousing"          "animation"            "anomalize"  
... this goes on
```

I would instead propose that a folder such as `/opt/rpkgs/<Rversion>` be created and the packages installed there then in Rprofile.site set `.libPaths(<pathtothat>)` however there might be some other quirks I have to dredge up from memory if we go down this path. In particular there are some configuration incantations that do things like stop the autocreation of the home library. I spent a long time finding the right pattern ~ 2 years ago but would want to re-up that knowledge before we locked into a specific pattern.

title: Bump R, Python versions and R package snapshots
description:
- [x] Alter 202111 version to 202205
- [x] Change latest R in the image to _actual latest R_
- [x] Choose a snapshot for the new R version
- [x] Change alternate R to the "currently latest in image"
- [x] Change alternate R snapshot to be the "currently latest in image" snapshot (reproducibility)
- [x] Change latest python in the image to _actual latest Python_
- [x] Change alternate python to "latest python in the image"
- [x] Merge PR

Then:
- [x] Update Daemonset to pull latest image
- [x] Update RSW to reference latest image
- [x] Test and be sure that things work!
